rawProviderIdea.title: Wrong-Room Light Switch
rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Flipping switch controls nearest room's light.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: The switch controls the light in a different room (e.g., bathroom), while the room you're in stays dark; each switch in house controls a random other room.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Kiko flips living room switch; hall light turns on, living room dark.
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Light switches are spatially tied to their room; cross-wiring makes them useless for local control.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to illuminate your room instead lights a distant room, leaving you in dark.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Kiko stands in dark living room flipping a switch; through the doorway, the bathroom light is on, and the living room remains dark.

beats.strategy: Kiko flips the switch repeatedly, hoping to get the right room.
beats.visibleConsequence: Various lights in the house turn on and off in a pattern, but the living room stays dark while the porch light blinks.
beats.newInformation: The switch cycles through all other rooms except the one he's in.

beats.strategy: Kiko walks to the bathroom to flip that switch.
beats.visibleConsequence: The bathroom light turns off, and the living room light turns on.
beats.newInformation: Switches are paired with opposite rooms; you must be in the room you don't want lit.

beats.strategy: Kiko stands in the doorway between rooms to flip both switches.
beats.visibleConsequence: Both rooms go dark, and a flickering light appears in the attic.
beats.newInformation: Simultaneous toggles transfer power to an unswitched room.

beats.strategy: Kiko uses a flashlight to see while navigating the switch panel.
beats.visibleConsequence: The flashlight turns on, but its beam illuminates the wrong room through a window, and Kiko stumbles.
beats.newInformation: The cross-wiring extends to all light sources, including portable ones.

beats.strategy: Kiko gives up and uses candles.
beats.visibleConsequence: The candles' flames cast shadows that point to a hidden switch behind a bookshelf; flipping that switch turns on the sun outside, causing full daylight indoors.
beats.newInformation: There is a master switch that controls daylight, not indoor lights, solving the darkness but at absurd scale.

rawProviderIdea.finalPayoff: The candles' flames cast shadows that point to a hidden switch behind a bookshelf; flipping that switch turns on the sun outside, causing full daylight indoors.
rawProviderIdea.suggestedPayoffFamily: unexpected causal success via wrong switch
rawProviderIdea.loopPotential: The daylight switch may reset at night, forcing Kiko to find another hidden control.
rawProviderIdea.providerRationale: Light switch's local function is scrambled; intuitive because you see wrong room light up.

beats.description: Kiko stands in dark living room flipping a switch; through the doorway, the bathroom light is on, and the living room remains dark. Kiko Kiko flips the switch repeatedly, hoping to get the right room.. Various lights in the house turn on and off in a pattern, but the living room stays dark while the porch light blinks. The switch cycles through all other rooms except the one he's in.

Kiko Kiko walks to the bathroom to flip that switch.. The bathroom light turns off, and the living room light turns on. Switches are paired with opposite rooms; you must be in the room you don't want lit.
Kiko Kiko stands in the doorway between rooms to flip both switches.. Both rooms go dark, and a flickering light appears in the attic. Simultaneous toggles transfer power to an unswitched room.

Kiko Kiko uses a flashlight to see while navigating the switch panel.. The flashlight turns on, but its beam illuminates the wrong room through a window, and Kiko stumbles. The cross-wiring extends to all light sources, including portable ones.

Kiko Kiko gives up and uses candles.. The candles' flames cast shadows that point to a hidden switch behind a bookshelf; flipping that switch turns on the sun outside, causing full daylight indoors. There is a master switch that controls daylight, not indoor lights, solving the darkness but at absurd scale.

The switch cycles through all other rooms except the one he's in.

rawProviderIdea.title: Collapsing Chair
rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Chair supports weight when sat on.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: The chair remains rigid when empty, but the instant any weight is applied, its legs fold flat, dropping occupant to floor; when empty, it pops back upright.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Arda sits, chair flattens beneath him.
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Chair's structural function is support; conditional collapse makes sitting impossible.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action of sitting triggers the loss of support, so you can never rest in chair.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Arda is mid-air just above a chair that has collapsed flat on the floor, legs splayed outward.

beats.strategy: Arda checks the chair, stands it up, and presses on the seat with one hand.
beats.visibleConsequence: The chair collapses instantly under the light hand pressure, then springs back.
beats.newInformation: Even partial weight triggers collapse; no weight means rigid.

beats.strategy: Arda tries to sit very slowly, easing weight onto the seat.
beats.visibleConsequence: The chair collapses progressively, lowering him to the floor in a controlled slide, then snaps shut on his fingers.
beats.newInformation: Slow approach doesn't prevent collapse; it just prolongs the drop.

beats.strategy: Arda puts a stack of books on the chair to hold it steady.
beats.visibleConsequence: The chair stays upright, but when Arda sits on the books, the chair collapses sideways and books scatter.
beats.newInformation: Distributed weight still triggers collapse as long as it includes Arda.

beats.strategy: Arda stands on the chair instead of sitting.
beats.visibleConsequence: The chair flings him forward like a catapult, launching him onto the desk.
beats.newInformation: The chair's collapse mechanism can store and release energy when weight is applied.

beats.strategy: Arda gives up and sits on the floor.
beats.visibleConsequence: The chair, now empty, creeps over and positions itself under him, then collapses flat, leaving him sitting on a folded chair.
beats.newInformation: The chair is attracted to being sat on but cannot support, so it ends up as a flattened seat.

rawProviderIdea.finalPayoff: The chair, now empty, creeps over and positions itself under him, then collapses flat, leaving him sitting on a folded chair.
rawProviderIdea.suggestedPayoffFamily: object agency / goal partially achieved absurdly
rawProviderIdea.loopPotential: Arda might use a different chair, but the same collapse rule may apply to its twin.
rawProviderIdea.providerRationale: Chair's support function is conditionally removed; visible collapse on sitting is classic but we vary with self-moving chair.

normalizedConcept.title: Collapsing Chair
normalizedConcept.impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction: The chair remains rigid when empty, but the instant any weight is applied, its legs fold flat, dropping occupant to floor; when empty, it pops back upright.
normalizedConcept.frameZeroDescription: Arda is mid-air just above a chair that has collapsed flat on the floor, legs splayed outward. Arda Arda checks the chair, stands it up, and presses on the seat with one hand.. The chair collapses instantly under the light hand pressure, then springs back. Even partial weight triggers collapse; no weight means rigid.

escalationPlan.description: Arda is mid-air just above a chair that has collapsed flat on the floor, legs splayed outward. Arda Arda checks the chair, stands it up, and presses on the seat with one hand.. The chair collapses instantly under the light hand pressure, then springs back. Even partial weight triggers collapse; no weight means rigid.

Arda Arda tries to sit very slowly, easing weight onto the seat.. The chair collapses progressively, lowering him to the floor in a controlled slide, then snaps shut on his fingers. Slow approach doesn't prevent collapse; it just prolongs the drop.

Arda Arda puts a stack of books on the chair to hold it steady.. The chair stays upright, but when Arda sits on the books, the chair collapses sideways and books scatter. Distributed weight still triggers collapse as long as it includes Arda.

Arda Arda stands on the chair instead of sitting.. The chair flings him forward like a catapult, launching him onto the desk. The chair's collapse mechanism can store and release energy when weight is applied.

Arda Arda gives up and sits on the floor.. The chair, now empty, creeps over and positions itself under him, then collapses flat, leaving him sitting on a folded chair. The chair is attracted to being sat on but cannot support, so it ends up as a flattened seat.

normalizedConcept.finalPayoff: Arda Arda gives up and sits on the floor.. The chair, now empty, creeps over and positions itself under him, then collapses flat, leaving him sitting on a folded chair. The chair is attracted to being sat on but cannot support, so it ends up as a flattened seat.

rawProviderIdea.title: Book Jumps to End
rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Opening book at page 1 shows beginning.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: Whenever you try to read from the beginning, the pages turn themselves rapidly to the last page; the text also rearranges so the story reads backward from end to start.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Noah opens book at page 1; pages flip to end, and the first words are 'The End.'
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Book is meant to be read sequentially; if it forces you to the end, reading the start is impossible.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action of reading from page 1 triggers skipping to end, preventing normal progress.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Noah holds a book open, but the pages are a blur, and the visible page shows the final chapter with 'The End' at the bottom.

beats.strategy: Noah holds the first page down with his thumb and tries to read.
beats.visibleConsequence: The pages underneath ripple and flip, pushing his thumb out and snapping the book shut.
beats.newInformation: The book can generate internal wind to turn pages.

beats.strategy: Noah starts reading from the end, hoping the reversed story still makes sense.
beats.visibleConsequence: The text on the last page reads normally, but when he turns back one page, the words are upside down.
beats.newInformation: Reading backward causes alternating page orientations.

beats.strategy: Noah uses a bookmark to keep the page, but the bookmark is ejected like a projectile.
beats.visibleConsequence: The book opens to a random middle page, and the story is now a recipe for soup.
beats.newInformation: The book's content changes based on which page is forced open.

beats.strategy: Noah photocopies page 1 and reads the copy.
beats.visibleConsequence: The copy's text disappears, and the book's page 1 becomes blank.
beats.newInformation: The book can transfer its text to any copy and then erase it.

beats.strategy: Noah closes the book and listens to an audiobook instead.
beats.visibleConsequence: The audiobook begins with the final chapter, and the physical book flips pages in sync with the audio, ending in 3 seconds.
beats.newInformation: The impossible rule extends to all versions of the story.

rawProviderIdea.finalPayoff: The audiobook begins with the final chapter, and the physical book flips pages in sync with the audio, ending in 3 seconds.
rawProviderIdea.loopPotential: Any attempt to experience the story from the beginning will be skipped to the end.
rawProviderIdea.providerRationale: Book's sequential reading is inverted by auto-flipping to end; visually clear with page blur.

rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Laces tie into a bow that stays.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: As you tie a bow, the laces weave themselves into additional knots, becoming tighter and more complex with every pull; untying creates two new knots.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Opa ties a simple bow; the laces instantly form a cloverleaf knot.
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Laces are meant to secure shoe with a single bow; self-knotting prevents both tying and untying.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action of tying laces overcomplicates them, making shoes impossible to put on or remove.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Opa sits on a bench with one shoe on, but the laces are a mass of tangled knots covering the shoe.

beats.strategy: Opa pulls one end to untangle the knot.
beats.visibleConsequence: The laces form a figure-eight around his ankle, tightening the shoe.
beats.newInformation: Pulling any lace end adds a new knot and tightens.

beats.strategy: Opa uses a fork to pick apart the knots.
beats.visibleConsequence: The fork gets woven into the laces, and the shoe jumps off his foot, still knotted with fork.
beats.newInformation: Tools get incorporated into the self-knotting laces.

beats.strategy: Opa removes the shoe and works on it in his lap.
beats.visibleConsequence: The laces knot around his fingers, tying his hands to the shoe.
beats.newInformation: The laces can target body parts as new knots.

beats.strategy: Opa puts the shoe under running water to loosen fibers.

beats.newInformation: Water worsens the knots due to shrinking.

beats.strategy: Opa gives up and walks barefoot.

beats.newInformation: The laces only cooperate when no one is touching them, and they switch shoes.

normalizedConcept.title: Bending Nail Hammer
normalizedConcept.impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction: Every hammer strike causes the nail to bend away from the wall at a right angle; bending increases with force.
normalizedConcept.frameZeroDescription: Kiko holds hammer mid-swing, but the nail protruding from the wall is bent into a U-shape, and the picture frame leans beside him. Kiko Kiko holds the nail straight with pliers and hammers gently.. The nail bends around the pliers and grips them, trapping the tool. The nail's bending is directional and can ensnare nearby tools.

escalationPlan.description: Kiko holds hammer mid-swing, but the nail protruding from the wall is bent into a U-shape, and the picture frame leans beside him. Kiko Kiko holds the nail straight with pliers and hammers gently.. The nail bends around the pliers and grips them, trapping the tool. The nail's bending is directional and can ensnare nearby tools.
Kiko Kiko uses a longer nail, hoping it will go straight.. The long nail curls into a spiral, then springs back and pings off the wall. Nail length increases elasticity, causing projectile bending.
Kiko Kiko pre-drills a hole, then taps the nail.. The nail passes halfway, then bends sideways and splits the wallboard, making a large hole. The nail bends at a specific depth, damaging the wall.

Kiko Kiko gives up on nails and uses adhesive strips.. The hammer leaps from his hand, straightens the bent nail with one tap, then hammers it perfectly into the wall. The hammer can install nails only when not held by Kiko.

Kiko Kiko grabs the hammer to adjust the picture, but the hammer now bends every nail in the house.. All nails in the room curve, pictures crash, and the original nail pings into Kiko's hand, bending his thumb comically. The hammer's bent-nail effect spreads to all previously straight nails.

normalizedConcept.finalPayoff: Kiko Kiko grabs the hammer to adjust the picture, but the hammer now bends every nail in the house.. rawProviderIdea.title: Opposite-Color Paintbrush
rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Brush applies paint color loaded on it.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: Whatever color you load, the brush deposits the complementary color; loading blue paints orange, loading red paints green.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Mimi strokes blue paint; wall turns orange.
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Brush is a transfer tool for pigment; if it inverts color, painting a chosen color is impossible.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to apply blue paint produces orange, so the wall never becomes blue.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Mimi stands at a wall with a blue paint bucket and brush mid-stroke; the painted patch is vivid orange.

beats.strategy: Mimi mixes a custom color equal parts blue and orange, hoping inversion cancels.
beats.visibleConsequence: The brush paints a shimmering gray that immediately splits into blue and orange stripes.
beats.newInformation: Complementary inversion doesn't cancel but separates into two colors.

beats.strategy: Mimi tries to paint the wall orange, expecting inversion to give blue.
beats.visibleConsequence: The wall turns blue-green, not pure blue, and the brush swirls automatically.
beats.newInformation: The inversion rule includes a hue shift, so aiming for orange doesn't yield blue.

beats.strategy: Mimi uses a roller instead of brush.
beats.visibleConsequence: The roller paints the opposite color at triple scale, covering the wall in a giant orange sunburst.
beats.newInformation: The inversion applies to any painting tool, increasing area.

beats.strategy: Mimi puts a stencil on the wall to paint a pattern.
beats.visibleConsequence: The stencil areas stay original color, while the exposed wall turns complementary, creating a negative of the pattern.
beats.newInformation: The brush inverts color in the open areas, not just strokes.

beats.strategy: Mimi gives up and paints the wall back white.
beats.visibleConsequence: The white paint turns black, then the entire wall flashes and becomes a mirror reflecting the room in inverted colors.
beats.newInformation: Painting white triggers a full-wall color inversion, turning the wall into a funhouse mirror.

rawProviderIdea.finalPayoff: The white paint turns black, then the entire wall flashes and becomes a mirror reflecting the room in inverted colors.
rawProviderIdea.loopPotential: Any new paint attempt may cause new color chaos; the wall can never be one color.
rawProviderIdea.providerRationale: Paintbrush's pigment transfer is inverted; visually clear when blue becomes orange.

normalizedConcept.title: Opposite-Color Paintbrush
normalizedConcept.impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction: Whatever color you load, the brush deposits the complementary color; loading blue paints orange, loading red paints green.
normalizedConcept.frameZeroDescription: Mimi stands at a wall with a blue paint bucket and brush mid-stroke; the painted patch is vivid orange. Mimi Mimi mixes a custom color equal parts blue and orange, hoping inversion cancels.. The brush paints a shimmering gray that immediately splits into blue and orange stripes. Complementary inversion doesn't cancel but separates into two colors.

escalationPlan.description: Mimi stands at a wall with a blue paint bucket and brush mid-stroke; the painted patch is vivid orange. Mimi Mimi mixes a custom color equal parts blue and orange, hoping inversion cancels.. The brush paints a shimmering gray that immediately splits into blue and orange stripes. Complementary inversion doesn't cancel but separates into two colors.

Mimi Mimi tries to paint the wall orange, expecting inversion to give blue.. The wall turns blue-green, not pure blue, and the brush swirls automatically. The inversion rule includes a hue shift, so aiming for orange doesn't yield blue.

Mimi Mimi uses a roller instead of brush.. The roller paints the opposite color at triple scale, covering the wall in a giant orange sunburst. The inversion applies to any painting tool, increasing area.

Mimi Mimi puts a stencil on the wall to paint a pattern.. The stencil areas stay original color, while the exposed wall turns complementary, creating a negative of the pattern. The brush inverts color in the open areas, not just strokes.

Mimi Mimi gives up and paints the wall back white.. The white paint turns black, then the entire wall flashes and becomes a mirror reflecting the room in inverted colors. Painting white triggers a full-wall color inversion, turning the wall into a funhouse mirror.

normalizedConcept.finalPayoff: Mimi Mimi gives up and paints the wall back white.. The white paint turns black, then the entire wall flashes and becomes a mirror reflecting the room in inverted colors. Painting white triggers a full-wall color inversion, turning the wall into a funhouse mirror.

The brush paints a shimmering gray that immediately splits into blue and orange stripes. Complementary inversion doesn't cancel but separates into two colors.
3-6s: Mimi Mimi tries to paint the wall orange, expecting inversion to give blue.. The wall turns blue-green, not pure blue, and the brush swirls automatically. The inversion rule includes a hue shift, so aiming for orange doesn't yield blue.
6-9s: Mimi Mimi uses a roller instead of brush.. The roller paints the opposite color at triple scale, covering the wall in a giant orange sunburst. The inversion applies to any painting tool, increasing area.

rawProviderIdea.title: Dirtying Washing Machine
rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Clothes come out cleaner.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: The machine extracts dirt from clothes and redeposits it onto another item in the same load, so the load comes out with one clean item and the rest soot-black.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Arda opens washer, one white shirt pristine, other clothes blackened.
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Washer is meant to remove dirt; if it just moves dirt between items, cleaning is incomplete.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to wash clothes leaves most dirtier, preventing clean laundry.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Arda looks into open washing machine; a single clean white shirt sits atop a pile of blackened garments.

beats.strategy: Arda separates whites and colors, running two loads.
beats.visibleConsequence: In the white load, dirt migrates to the machine's drum, which turns black and rubs off on all whites.
beats.newInformation: The machine can hold and transfer dirt to its own walls.

beats.strategy: Arda puts all clothes in with extra detergent.
beats.visibleConsequence: The detergent bubbles turn gray, and the clothes come out tie-dyed with dirt patterns.
beats.newInformation: More detergent spreads dirt more evenly, creating stains.

beats.strategy: Arda wipes the drum clean before running again.
beats.visibleConsequence: The wiped drum stays clean, but the clothes now emerge with mud splatters exactly where fabric touched the drum.
beats.newInformation: The machine deposits dirt at contact points, so any cycle dirties.

beats.strategy: Arda uses a mesh laundry bag to isolate each item.
beats.visibleConsequence: Each bag becomes a dirt packet; one bag bursts, sprinkling dry dirt like a pepper shaker.
beats.newInformation: Isolating clothes turns each into a dirt bomb.

beats.strategy: Arda gives up and takes clothes to a river to wash by hand.
beats.visibleConsequence: The washing machine follows him on its spin cycle, rolling down the street, and the clothes he washed in the river absorb dirt from the machine's wake.
beats.newInformation: The machine pursues Arda and re-dirties any clothes he cleans elsewhere.

rawProviderIdea.finalPayoff: The washing machine follows him on its spin cycle, rolling down the street, and the clothes he washed in the river absorb dirt from the machine's wake.
rawProviderIdea.loopPotential: Any washing attempt, anywhere, attracts the machine's dirt.
rawProviderIdea.providerRationale: Washer's cleaning function is reversed into dirt redistribution; visually obvious with one clean item among blackened.

normalizedConcept.title: Dirtying Washing Machine
normalizedConcept.impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction: The machine extracts dirt from clothes and redeposits it onto another item in the same load, so the load comes out with one clean item and the rest soot-black.
normalizedConcept.frameZeroDescription: Arda looks into open washing machine; a single clean white shirt sits atop a pile of blackened garments. Arda Arda separates whites and colors, running two loads.. In the white load, dirt migrates to the machine's drum, which turns black and rubs off on all whites. The machine can hold and transfer dirt to its own walls.

escalationPlan.description: Arda looks into open washing machine; a single clean white shirt sits atop a pile of blackened garments. Arda Arda separates whites and colors, running two loads.. In the white load, dirt migrates to the machine's drum, which turns black and rubs off on all whites. The machine can hold and transfer dirt to its own walls.
Arda Arda puts all clothes in with extra detergent.. The detergent bubbles turn gray, and the clothes come out tie-dyed with dirt patterns. More detergent spreads dirt more evenly, creating stains.

Arda Arda wipes the drum clean before running again.. The wiped drum stays clean, but the clothes now emerge with mud splatters exactly where fabric touched the drum. The machine deposits dirt at contact points, so any cycle dirties.
Arda Arda uses a mesh laundry bag to isolate each item.. Each bag becomes a dirt packet; one bag bursts, sprinkling dry dirt like a pepper shaker. Isolating clothes turns each into a dirt bomb.

Arda Arda gives up and takes clothes to a river to wash by hand.. The washing machine follows him on its spin cycle, rolling down the street, and the clothes he washed in the river absorb dirt from the machine's wake. The machine pursues Arda and re-dirties any clothes he cleans elsewhere.

normalizedConcept.finalPayoff: Arda Arda gives up and takes clothes to a river to wash by hand.. The washing machine follows him on its spin cycle, rolling down the street, and the clothes he washed in the river absorb dirt from the machine's wake. The machine pursues Arda and re-dirties any clothes he cleans elsewhere.

rawProviderIdea.title: Spiky Ice Cube Tray
rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Water in tray freezes into cube shapes.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: The water freezes into sharp upward spikes that puncture the plastic tray and any covering, growing toward the ceiling.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Noah opens freezer, ice spikes have pierced the tray and are growing out.
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Ice tray forms cubes via expansion; if freezing instead creates directional spikes, ice is unusable and sharp-looking.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to make cubes results in spiky ice that cannot be extracted safely, preventing cold drink.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Noah opens freezer; a tray is pierced by icy spikes pointing upward like a hedgehog.

beats.strategy: Noah tries to break off a spike by hand.
beats.visibleConsequence: The spike snaps but instantly regrows longer and sharper, nicking the freezer shelf.
beats.newInformation: The ice regrows when broken, faster each time.

beats.strategy: Noah runs warm water over the tray to melt spikes.
beats.visibleConsequence: The spikes melt into a small flood that refreezes into an even larger spike cluster on the counter.
beats.newInformation: Melted water refreezes into spikes anywhere, not just tray.

beats.strategy: Noah places the tray upside down in the freezer, hoping spikes grow downward.
beats.visibleConsequence: The spikes grow upward relative to gravity, piercing through the tray bottom and sticking out the top.
beats.newInformation: The spike growth is gravity-independent, always along the vertical axis of the tray's original orientation.

beats.strategy: Noah uses a different silicone tray to make cubes.
beats.visibleConsequence: The silicone stretches around the spikes, forming a balloon that inflates until it pops, scattering ice shards.
beats.newInformation: Flexible trays can't contain the spikes; they stretch into a balloon.

beats.strategy: Noah gives up and buys a bag of ice from the store.
beats.visibleConsequence: The bag of ice starts sprouting spikes inside the plastic bag, and the bag floats up to the ceiling, freezing a chandelier.
beats.newInformation: The spike formation follows any purchased ice, spreading to the environment.

rawProviderIdea.finalPayoff: The bag of ice starts sprouting spikes inside the plastic bag, and the bag floats up to the ceiling, freezing a chandelier.
rawProviderIdea.loopPotential: Any future ice-making or ice-buying will produce spikes, so cold drinks become impossible.
rawProviderIdea.providerRationale: Ice cube tray's freezing function is subverted into spike growth; visually dramatic and blocks use.

Noah Noah runs warm water over the tray to melt spikes.. The spikes melt into a small flood that refreezes into an even larger spike cluster on the counter. Melted water refreezes into spikes anywhere, not just tray.

Noah Noah places the tray upside down in the freezer, hoping spikes grow downward.. The spikes grow upward relative to gravity, piercing through the tray bottom and sticking out the top. The spike growth is gravity-independent, always along the vertical axis of the tray's original orientation.

Noah Noah uses a different silicone tray to make cubes.. The silicone stretches around the spikes, forming a balloon that inflates until it pops, scattering ice shards. Flexible trays can't contain the spikes; they stretch into a balloon.

Noah Noah gives up and buys a bag of ice from the store.. The bag of ice starts sprouting spikes inside the plastic bag, and the bag floats up to the ceiling, freezing a chandelier. The spike formation follows any purchased ice, spreading to the environment.

rawProviderIdea.title: Shadow Flashlight
rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Flashlight produces light beam to illuminate.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: The flashlight absorbs light and projects a darkness beam; pointing it at objects makes them disappear into shadow, while surroundings stay dim.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Opa turns on flashlight, a black cone shoots out, making the area darker.
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Flashlight's purpose is to emit light; emitting darkness is its inverse.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to illuminate keys instead casts them into deeper shadow, preventing search.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Opa points a flashlight at the floor, but a black beam covers the area where keys should be, while the rest of the room is faint.

beats.strategy: Opa shakes the flashlight and changes batteries.
beats.visibleConsequence: The darkness beam becomes wider, swallowing a chair and half the room into blackness.
beats.newInformation: More power increases darkness, not light.

beats.strategy: Opa points the flashlight at the ceiling, hoping reflected light reveals keys.
beats.visibleConsequence: The ceiling turns black and starts dripping shadow like ink, covering the floor.
beats.newInformation: The darkness is a substance that can drip and spread.

beats.strategy: Opa turns on a lamp instead.
beats.visibleConsequence: The lamp works normally, but the flashlight's shadow beam seeks out the lamp and extinguishes it.
beats.newInformation: The darkness beam actively cancels any other light source.

beats.strategy: Opa uses the flashlight in reverse, pointing it at his own eyes.
beats.visibleConsequence: Instead of darkness, a bright beam shines out the back of the flashlight, illuminating a corner where keys are visible.
beats.newInformation: The flashlight has reversed polarity: front emits dark, back emits light.

beats.strategy: Opa picks up the keys using the light from the back.
beats.visibleConsequence: The keys glow and float into the flashlight's front beam, where they vanish into shadow, never to be found.
beats.newInformation: The flashlight's front beam can erase objects, not just darken them.

rawProviderIdea.finalPayoff: The keys glow and float into the flashlight's front beam, where they vanish into shadow, never to be found.
rawProviderIdea.loopPotential: The keys might reappear if Opa uses the back beam, but then the front beam may erase them again.
rawProviderIdea.providerRationale: Flashlight's light emission is inverted to shadow projection; intuitive and blocks finding keys.

normalizedConcept.title: Shadow Flashlight

normalizedConcept.frameZeroDescription: Opa points a flashlight at the floor, but a black beam covers the area where keys should be, while the rest of the room is faint. Opa Opa shakes the flashlight and changes batteries.. The darkness beam becomes wider, swallowing a chair and half the room into blackness. More power increases darkness, not light.

Opa Opa shakes the flashlight and changes batteries.. The darkness beam becomes wider, swallowing a chair and half the room into blackness. More power increases darkness, not light.

Opa Opa points the flashlight at the ceiling, hoping reflected light reveals keys.. The ceiling turns black and starts dripping shadow like ink, covering the floor. The darkness is a substance that can drip and spread.

Opa Opa picks up the keys using the light from the back.. The keys glow and float into the flashlight's front beam, where they vanish into shadow, never to be found. The flashlight's front beam can erase objects, not just darken them.

rawProviderIdea.title: Delayed Mirror
rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Mirror shows real-time reflection.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: The mirror shows a reflection delayed by one second, so Kiko sees her previous movement; when she moves to adjust, the lag causes her to misreach and bump herself.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Kiko raises hand, mirror's hand raises a second later.
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Mirror's function is immediate visual feedback; delay makes self-grooming impossible.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to style hair is based on outdated visual, so hands miss, preventing fixing.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Kiko stands before mirror, her hand raised, but the reflection's hand is still lowered; a ghostly lag overlay is visible.

beats.strategy: Kiko moves slowly, watching the mirror to adjust to delay.
beats.visibleConsequence: The mirror's delay increases to three seconds, and her reflection starts combing hair that Kiko hasn't touched yet.
beats.newInformation: The lag can grow when she tries to compensate.

beats.strategy: Kiko touches her hair while looking down, ignoring the mirror.
beats.visibleConsequence: The mirror shows her reflection looking up and smiling, then her own head tilts involuntarily to match.
beats.newInformation: The delayed reflection can control her current actions, not just display.

beats.strategy: Kiko covers the mirror with a towel.
beats.visibleConsequence: The covered mirror continues to reflect, showing a delayed image on the towel's surface like a screen.
beats.newInformation: The reflection can project onto coverings.

beats.strategy: Kiko turns the mirror around to face the wall.
beats.visibleConsequence: The back of the mirror shows a live feed of Kiko from a second ago on the wall, and she sees herself walking backward.
beats.newInformation: The mirror's delay effect transfers to the wall surface.

beats.strategy: Kiko stands perfectly still until the reflection catches up.
beats.visibleConsequence: The reflection catches up and then freezes, while Kiko's own image splits into two identical Kikos in the room.
beats.newInformation: Synchronizing the delay creates a duplicate Kiko, solving the grooming by having the duplicate fix her hair.

rawProviderIdea.finalPayoff: The reflection catches up and then freezes, while Kiko's own image splits into two identical Kikos in the room.
rawProviderIdea.loopPotential: The duplicate Kiko may also have a delayed reflection, causing infinite twins.
rawProviderIdea.providerRationale: Mirror's real-time reflection is subverted by lag; visually clear when movements don't match.

normalizedConcept.title: Delayed Mirror
normalizedConcept.impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction: The mirror shows a reflection delayed by one second, so Kiko sees her previous movement; when she moves to adjust, the lag causes her to misreach and bump herself.
normalizedConcept.frameZeroDescription: Kiko stands before mirror, her hand raised, but the reflection's hand is still lowered; a ghostly lag overlay is visible. Kiko Kiko moves slowly, watching the mirror to adjust to delay.. The mirror's delay increases to three seconds, and her reflection starts combing hair that Kiko hasn't touched yet. The lag can grow when she tries to compensate.

escalationPlan.description: Kiko stands before mirror, her hand raised, but the reflection's hand is still lowered; a ghostly lag overlay is visible. Kiko Kiko moves slowly, watching the mirror to adjust to delay.. The mirror's delay increases to three seconds, and her reflection starts combing hair that Kiko hasn't touched yet. The lag can grow when she tries to compensate.

Kiko Kiko touches her hair while looking down, ignoring the mirror.. The mirror shows her reflection looking up and smiling, then her own head tilts involuntarily to match. The delayed reflection can control her current actions, not just display.

rawProviderIdea.title: Swapping Stairs
rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Stairs have uniform riser heights, easy to climb.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: The stair heights rearrange each step you take: the step you are about to step on moves up or down, alternating between 1 inch and 3 feet, causing missteps.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Mimi steps on first stair; the second stair rises to waist height.
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Stairs are meant to offer predictable vertical increments; randomizing heights makes climbing impossible without tripping.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action of climbing is undermined by changing step dimensions, preventing reaching top.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Mimi is mid-climb, one foot on a low step, the next step has risen to her waist, while another step behind has sunk to floor level.

beats.strategy: Mimi tries to step over the high step onto the next.
beats.visibleConsequence: The high step sinks as she lifts her leg, causing her to stomp down hard and stumble.
beats.newInformation: The stairs anticipate her movement and adjust to keep her off balance.

beats.strategy: Mimi crawls on hands and knees to distribute weight.
beats.visibleConsequence: The steps flatten to a ramp, then tilt sideways, sliding her toward the wall.
beats.newInformation: The staircase can morph into different configurations.

beats.strategy: Mimi holds the railing and leaps up two steps.
beats.visibleConsequence: The steps she skipped fold up like a ladder, pinning her leg briefly, and the next flight appears as a spiral.
beats.newInformation: Skipping steps causes them to fold into obstacles.

beats.strategy: Mimi backs down and tries the escalator-like conveyor setting (if any).
beats.visibleConsequence: The stairs start moving like an escalator but in reverse, taking her back to the ground floor.
beats.newInformation: The staircase has a direction setting that always opposes her desired direction.

beats.strategy: Mimi gives up and sits on the bottom step.
beats.visibleConsequence: The entire staircase folds into a flat ramp, and Mimi slides gently up to the bedroom door without using stairs.
beats.newInformation: The stairs become a ramp when not climbed, allowing effortless travel.

rawProviderIdea.finalPayoff: The entire staircase folds into a flat ramp, and Mimi slides gently up to the bedroom door without using stairs.
rawProviderIdea.loopPotential: If Mimi tries to use the ramp, it might revert to chaotic stairs.
rawProviderIdea.providerRationale: Stairs' predictable steps are randomized in height; visually clear and directly blocks climbing.

normalizedConcept.title: Swapping Stairs
normalizedConcept.impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction: The stair heights rearrange each step you take: the step you are about to step on moves up or down, alternating between 1 inch and 3 feet, causing missteps.
normalizedConcept.frameZeroDescription: Mimi is mid-climb, one foot on a low step, the next step has risen to her waist, while another step behind has sunk to floor level. Mimi Mimi tries to step over the high step onto the next.. The high step sinks as she lifts her leg, causing her to stomp down hard and stumble. The stairs anticipate her movement and adjust to keep her off balance.

escalationPlan.description: Mimi is mid-climb, one foot on a low step, the next step has risen to her waist, while another step behind has sunk to floor level. Mimi Mimi tries to step over the high step onto the next.. The high step sinks as she lifts her leg, causing her to stomp down hard and stumble. The stairs anticipate her movement and adjust to keep her off balance.
Mimi Mimi crawls on hands and knees to distribute weight.. The steps flatten to a ramp, then tilt sideways, sliding her toward the wall. The staircase can morph into different configurations.

Mimi Mimi holds the railing and leaps up two steps.. The steps she skipped fold up like a ladder, pinning her leg briefly, and the next flight appears as a spiral. Skipping steps causes them to fold into obstacles.

Mimi Mimi backs down and tries the escalator-like conveyor setting (if any).. The stairs start moving like an escalator but in reverse, taking her back to the ground floor. The staircase has a direction setting that always opposes her desired direction.

Mimi Mimi gives up and sits on the bottom step.. The entire staircase folds into a flat ramp, and Mimi slides gently up to the bedroom door without using stairs. The stairs become a ramp when not climbed, allowing effortless travel.

normalizedConcept.finalPayoff: Mimi Mimi gives up and sits on the bottom step.. The entire staircase folds into a flat ramp, and Mimi slides gently up to the bedroom door without using stairs. The stairs become a ramp when not climbed, allowing effortless travel.
normalizedConcept.evaluationText:

The high step sinks as she lifts her leg, causing her to stomp down hard and stumble. The stairs anticipate her movement and adjust to keep her off balance.
3-6s: Mimi Mimi crawls on hands and knees to distribute weight.. The steps flatten to a ramp, then tilt sideways, sliding her toward the wall. The staircase can morph into different configurations.
6-9s: Mimi Mimi holds the railing and leaps up two steps.. The steps she skipped fold up like a ladder, pinning her leg briefly, and the next flight appears as a spiral. Skipping steps causes them to fold into obstacles.
9-12s: Mimi Mimi backs down and tries the escalator-like conveyor setting (if any).. The stairs start moving like an escalator but in reverse, taking her back to the ground floor. The staircase has a direction setting that always opposes her desired direction.
12-15s: Mimi Mimi gives up and sits on the bottom step.. The entire staircase folds into a flat ramp, and Mimi slides gently up to the bedroom door without using stairs. The stairs become a ramp when not climbed, allowing effortless travel.

normalizedConcept.frameZeroDescription: Luca holds open wallet, a cloud of bills swirling around his head, while the wallet is empty. Luca Luca closes the wallet to get money back, then opens it just a crack.. The bills rocket out through the crack like a fan, hitting him in the face. The ejection force is proportional to how little opening there is.

escalationPlan.description: Luca holds open wallet, a cloud of bills swirling around his head, while the wallet is empty. Luca Luca closes the wallet to get money back, then opens it just a crack.. The bills rocket out through the crack like a fan, hitting him in the face. The ejection force is proportional to how little opening there is.
Luca Luca tries to grab a bill midair.. The bill slips through his fingers and joins a whirlwind above the counter. Money becomes frictionless when airborne.
Luca Luca holds the wallet upside down and opens, hoping bills fall into his hand.. The bills fly upward, sticking to the ceiling in a neat stack. Gravity is reversed for ejected money.
Luca Luca uses a debit card instead of cash.. The card also flies out and orbits the cashier's head like a boomerang. The ejection applies to any flat item in the wallet.

Luca Luca closes the wallet and hand it entire to the cashier.. The wallet opens itself in the cashier's hand, releasing all bills into a tip jar, and the card lands on the reader, approving payment. The wallet can pay by itself when given to the cashier, achieving the goal without Luca's control.

rawProviderIdea.title: Upward Flush Toilet
rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Flushing sends water and waste down into drain.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: Flushing causes water to shoot up from the bowl like a geyser, reaching the ceiling, and only after the flush stops does everything fall back into bowl.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Noah presses handle, water gushes upward, soaking him.
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Toilet's flush is gravity-fed downward; reversing flow makes it a fountain.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to flush creates an upward eruption, preventing clean and dry use.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Noah stands beside a toilet, a column of water shooting straight up from the bowl, while he shields his face.

beats.strategy: Noah closes the toilet lid before flushing.
beats.visibleConsequence: The lid blasts off, and the water column rockets to the ceiling, denting it.
beats.newInformation: The upward force is stronger than the lid.

beats.strategy: Noah flushes from a distance using a stick.
beats.visibleConsequence: The geyser follows the stick's movement, curving toward Noah and drenching him.
beats.newInformation: The water stream is attracted to the person flushing.

beats.strategy: Noah turns off the water supply valve behind the toilet.
beats.visibleConsequence: The geyser stops, but the toilet begins to shake and levitate, spinning slowly.
beats.newInformation: With no water, the toilet's internal pressure causes it to float.

beats.strategy: Noah tries using a plunger to redirect the water downward.
beats.visibleConsequence: The plunger gets sucked into the toilet, and the water forms a whirlpool that lifts the bathroom mat into the air.
beats.newInformation: The toilet can invert gravity for any loose object nearby.

beats.strategy: Noah gives up and leaves the bathroom.
beats.visibleConsequence: The toilet, still spinning, follows him, and all the water it previously shot up falls as indoor rain on the hallway.
beats.newInformation: The toilet's geyser water is delayed in falling and follows the toilet.

rawProviderIdea.finalPayoff: The toilet, still spinning, follows him, and all the water it previously shot up falls as indoor rain on the hallway.
rawProviderIdea.loopPotential: Any future flush will cause geyser and following rain; Noah may need an outhouse.
rawProviderIdea.providerRationale: Toilet's downward drainage is inverted into upward geyser; visually messy and blocks normal use.

beats.visual: Noah Noah flushes from a distance using a stick.. The geyser follows the stick's movement, curving toward Noah and drenching him. The water stream is attracted to the person flushing.

beats.quote: Noah Noah turns off the water supply valve behind the toilet.. The geyser stops, but the toilet begins to shake and levitate, spinning slowly. With no water, the toilet's internal pressure causes it to float.
beats.visual: Noah Noah turns off the water supply valve behind the toilet.. The geyser stops, but the toilet begins to shake and levitate, spinning slowly. With no water, the toilet's internal pressure causes it to float.

rawProviderIdea.title: Split Garbage Bag
rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Bag holds trash when tied and lifted.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: The bag remains intact in the can, but the moment you lift it, the seams split and trash falls back into the can; when you put bag back, it seals.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Opa lifts tied bag; bottom splits, trash drops.
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Garbage bag's containment is supposed to be stable under load; conditional splitting prevents removal.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to remove trash causes the bag to fail, so trash never leaves the can.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Opa holds the tied top of a garbage bag, but the bottom is wide open, trash spilling back into the can.

beats.strategy: Opa double-bags the trash with two bags.
beats.visibleConsequence: The outer bag splits, the inner bag holds, but then the inner bag's top unknots and trash flies out like a fountain.
beats.newInformation: Multiple bags shift the failure point rather than preventing it.

beats.strategy: Opa uses a box instead of a bag, tipping the trash into it.
beats.visibleConsequence: The box's bottom opens when Opa lifts it, dumping trash back into the can.
beats.newInformation: The rule applies to any container lifted with trash, not just bags.

beats.strategy: Opa scoops trash directly with a dustpan and carries it out.
beats.visibleConsequence: The dustpan flips upside down just before he reaches the door, scattering trash.
beats.newInformation: The anti-lifting rule extends to dustpans.

beats.strategy: Opa drags the entire trash can to the curb, not lifting anything.
beats.visibleConsequence: The can's wheels spin off, and the can anchors itself to the floor, refusing to move.
beats.newInformation: Moving trash without lifting is also blocked; the can self-anchors.

beats.strategy: Opa gives up and leaves the trash.
beats.visibleConsequence: The bag climbs out of the can, stretches over the trash, and seals it perfectly, then levitates to the curb.
beats.newInformation: The trash removes itself only when Opa stops trying.

rawProviderIdea.finalPayoff: The bag climbs out of the can, stretches over the trash, and seals it perfectly, then levitates to the curb.
rawProviderIdea.suggestedPayoffFamily: goal achieved by object after abandon
rawProviderIdea.loopPotential: If Opa tries to help next time, the bag will refuse again.
rawProviderIdea.providerRationale: Garbage bag's containment fails on lift; intuitive because you see bottom split and trash fall back.

normalizedConcept.title: Split Garbage Bag
normalizedConcept.impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction: The bag remains intact in the can, but the moment you lift it, the seams split and trash falls back into the can; when you put bag back, it seals.
normalizedConcept.frameZeroDescription: Opa holds the tied top of a garbage bag, but the bottom is wide open, trash spilling back into the can. Opa Opa double-bags the trash with two bags.. The outer bag splits, the inner bag holds, but then the inner bag's top unknots and trash flies out like a fountain. Multiple bags shift the failure point rather than preventing it.

escalationPlan.description: Opa holds the tied top of a garbage bag, but the bottom is wide open, trash spilling back into the can. Opa Opa double-bags the trash with two bags.. The outer bag splits, the inner bag holds, but then the inner bag's top unknots and trash flies out like a fountain. Multiple bags shift the failure point rather than preventing it.

Opa Opa uses a box instead of a bag, tipping the trash into it.. The box's bottom opens when Opa lifts it, dumping trash back into the can. The rule applies to any container lifted with trash, not just bags.
Opa Opa scoops trash directly with a dustpan and carries it out.. The dustpan flips upside down just before he reaches the door, scattering trash. The anti-lifting rule extends to dustpans.

Opa Opa drags the entire trash can to the curb, not lifting anything.. The can's wheels spin off, and the can anchors itself to the floor, refusing to move. Moving trash without lifting is also blocked; the can self-anchors.

Opa Opa gives up and leaves the trash.. The bag climbs out of the can, stretches over the trash, and seals it perfectly, then levitates to the curb. The trash removes itself only when Opa stops trying.

normalizedConcept.finalPayoff: Opa Opa gives up and leaves the trash.. The bag climbs out of the can, stretches over the trash, and seals it perfectly, then levitates to the curb. The trash removes itself only when Opa stops trying.

normalizedConcept.title: Disappearing Ink Pen
normalizedConcept.impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction: The pen writes visible ink, but the lines evaporate after exactly one second, leaving blank paper; when the pen is capped, the marks reappear on the paper in reverse order.
normalizedConcept.frameZeroDescription: Kiko holds a pen over a notepad; the word 'milk' is half-faded, the tail already invisible. Kiko Kiko writes quickly and photographs the list before it fades.. The photo also fades, and the phone's screen becomes blank where the list was. The disappearance transfers to any capture of the writing.

escalationPlan.description: Kiko holds a pen over a notepad; the word 'milk' is half-faded, the tail already invisible. Kiko Kiko writes quickly and photographs the list before it fades.. The photo also fades, and the phone's screen becomes blank where the list was. The disappearance transfers to any capture of the writing.
Kiko Kiko presses hard to dent paper so impressions remain.. The indentations flatten immediately, and the paper becomes smooth. The paper self-heals indents, erasing physical evidence.

Kiko Kiko writes with a different pen (pencil).. The pencil marks also vanish, and the pencil itself disappears while writing. The disappearing rule applies to all writing instruments, including the tool.

Kiko Kiko caps the pen and waits for marks to reappear.. The marks reappear in reverse order, forming a jumbled list that reads backwards from bottom to top. Capping the pen reverses time for the ink, but reverses the sequence.

Kiko Kiko reads the reversed list and heads to the store.. The list on paper rearranges to normal as she shops, but every item she picks up vanishes from the cart. The disappearing effect now applies to the actual items on the list, causing them to vanish when selected.

normalizedConcept.finalPayoff: Kiko Kiko reads the reversed list and heads to the store.. The list on paper rearranges to normal as she shops, but every item she picks up vanishes from the cart. The disappearing effect now applies to the actual items on the list, causing them to vanish when selected.

rawProviderIdea.title: Smearing Eraser
rawProviderIdea.normalExpectation: Eraser lifts graphite from paper.
rawProviderIdea.impossibleRule: Rubbing eraser spreads graphite into a larger smudge, and the smudge darkens into a sticky tar that stains fingers and paper.
rawProviderIdea.visibleTrigger: Mimi erases a line; it widens into a gray smear.
rawProviderIdea.whyThisObject: Eraser is designed to remove marks; if it smears, correcting mistakes is impossible.
rawProviderIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to erase makes the mistake bigger and messier, preventing correction.
rawProviderIdea.frameZeroDescription: Mimi holds an eraser on a paper; the erased area has turned into a dark smudge spreading outward.

beats.strategy: Mimi uses a clean corner of the eraser, pressing lightly.
beats.visibleConsequence: The smudge grows larger and darker, and the eraser corner becomes black.
beats.newInformation: The eraser absorbs graphite but redeposits it as tar.

beats.strategy: Mimi blows away the eraser shavings.
beats.visibleConsequence: The shavings fly up and stick to the paper, creating a swarm of black dots.
beats.newInformation: The tar-like graphite is airborne and attaches.

beats.strategy: Mimi tries to wipe the smudge with a tissue.
beats.visibleConsequence: The tissue sticks to the tar, then wads up and becomes a permanent black blob on the page.
beats.newInformation: Once smudged, the graphite becomes adhesive and traps cleaning tools.

beats.strategy: Mimi uses a white correction tape over the smudge.
beats.visibleConsequence: The tape turns black and peels off, pulling a layer of paper with it, leaving a hole.
beats.newInformation: The smudge corrodes any covering.

beats.strategy: Mimi gives up and closes the notebook.
beats.visibleConsequence: The smudge spreads to the opposite page, then shrinks into a perfect drawing of a cat, no longer a mistake.
beats.newInformation: When abandoned, the smudge transforms into a deliberate artwork, but not the intended correction.

rawProviderIdea.finalPayoff: The smudge spreads to the opposite page, then shrinks into a perfect drawing of a cat, no longer a mistake.
rawProviderIdea.loopPotential: If Mimi tries to replicate the cat, it may smear again.
rawProviderIdea.providerRationale: Eraser's removal function is inverted into smudging; visually obvious as the mark grows.

normalizedConcept.title: Smearing Eraser
normalizedConcept.impossibleRuleOrCoreContradiction: Rubbing eraser spreads graphite into a larger smudge, and the smudge darkens into a sticky tar that stains fingers and paper.
normalizedConcept.frameZeroDescription: Mimi holds an eraser on a paper; the erased area has turned into a dark smudge spreading outward. Mimi Mimi uses a clean corner of the eraser, pressing lightly.. The smudge grows larger and darker, and the eraser corner becomes black. The eraser absorbs graphite but redeposits it as tar.

escalationPlan.description: Mimi holds an eraser on a paper; the erased area has turned into a dark smudge spreading outward. Mimi Mimi uses a clean corner of the eraser, pressing lightly.. The smudge grows larger and darker, and the eraser corner becomes black. The eraser absorbs graphite but redeposits it as tar.
Mimi Mimi blows away the eraser shavings.. The shavings fly up and stick to the paper, creating a swarm of black dots. The tar-like graphite is airborne and attaches.

Mimi Mimi tries to wipe the smudge with a tissue.. The tissue sticks to the tar, then wads up and becomes a permanent black blob on the page. Once smudged, the graphite becomes adhesive and traps cleaning tools.
Mimi Mimi uses a white correction tape over the smudge.. The tape turns black and peels off, pulling a layer of paper with it, leaving a hole. The smudge corrodes any covering.

Mimi Mimi gives up and closes the notebook.. The smudge spreads to the opposite page, then shrinks into a perfect drawing of a cat, no longer a mistake. When abandoned, the smudge transforms into a deliberate artwork, but not the intended correction.

normalizedConcept.finalPayoff: Mimi Mimi gives up and closes the notebook.. The smudge spreads to the opposite page, then shrinks into a perfect drawing of a cat, no longer a mistake. When abandoned, the smudge transforms into a deliberate artwork, but not the intended correction.
normalizedConcept.evaluationText:
0-3s: Mimi holds an eraser on a paper; the erased area has turned into a dark smudge spreading outward. Mimi Mimi uses a clean corner of the eraser, pressing lightly.. The smudge grows larger and darker, and the eraser corner becomes black. The eraser absorbs graphite but redeposits it as tar.
3-6s: Mimi Mimi blows away the eraser shavings.. The shavings fly up and stick to the paper, creating a swarm of black dots. The tar-like graphite is airborne and attaches.
6-9s: Mimi Mimi tries to wipe the smudge with a tissue.. The tissue sticks to the tar, then wads up and becomes a permanent black blob on the page. Once smudged, the graphite becomes adhesive and traps cleaning tools.
9-12s: Mimi Mimi uses a white correction tape over the smudge.. The tape turns black and peels off, pulling a layer of paper with it, leaving a hole. The smudge corrodes any covering.
12-15s: Mimi Mimi gives up and closes the notebook.. The smudge spreads to the opposite page, then shrinks into a perfect drawing of a cat, no longer a mistake. When abandoned, the smudge transforms into a deliberate artwork, but not the intended correction.

providerRawIdea.title: Self-Healing Paper
providerRawIdea.normalExpectation: Scissors shear paper into two pieces.
providerRawIdea.impossibleRule: As scissors cut, the paper immediately heals behind the blades, leaving no cut; the scissors themselves become slightly more blunt.
providerRawIdea.visibleTrigger: Kiko snips a paper, the cut line closes seamlessly.
providerRawIdea.whyThisObject: Scissors are meant to divide material; if the material self-heals, the cutting action is futile.
providerRawIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The intended cut never persists, so crafting cannot proceed.
providerRawIdea.frameZeroDescription: Kiko holds scissors mid-snip on a paper; the cut line behind the blades is sealing itself closed, with no separation visible.

beats.strategy: Kiko cuts faster, moving scissors along a straight line.
beats.visibleConsequence: The paper zips back together instantly, and the scissors make a zipper-like sound.
beats.newInformation: Speed of cutting increases the healing speed equally.

beats.strategy: Kiko folds the paper and cuts through multiple layers.
beats.visibleConsequence: The layers fuse together at the cut line, creating a thicker uncut stack.
beats.newInformation: Cutting multiple layers causes them to weld, not separate.

beats.strategy: Kiko uses a craft knife instead of scissors.
beats.visibleConsequence: The knife blade passes through but the paper instantly reattaches, and the knife's edge dulls to a butter knife shape.
beats.newInformation: The self-healing effect applies to any cutting tool and dulls the blade.

beats.strategy: Kiko tries to tear the paper by hand.
beats.visibleConsequence: The paper stretches like rubber and bounces back, flipping out of his hands.
beats.newInformation: The paper has become elastic, so it cannot be cut or torn.

beats.strategy: Kiko gives up and tries to use pre-cut paper shapes from a packet.
beats.visibleConsequence: The pre-cut shapes snap back into full sheets, and the scissors in his hand leap to the paper and start 'cutting' but leaving no marks.
beats.newInformation: The rule reverses relationship: tools cuts but material refuses to remain divided; even pre-existing cuts are undone.

providerRawIdea.finalPayoff: The pre-cut shapes snap back into full sheets, and the scissors in his hand leap to the paper and start 'cutting' but leaving no marks.
providerRawIdea.loopPotential: Any future cutting attempt heals; Kiko might try water or fire, but risk of new escalation.
providerRawIdea.providerRationale: Scissors' dividing function is negated by self-healing paper; intuitive because cut line zips shut.

providerRawIdea.title: Self-Tucking Bed Sheets
providerRawIdea.everydayGoal: Get out of bed in the morning
providerRawIdea.normalExpectation: You push sheets off and stand up.
providerRawIdea.impossibleRule: The more you push sheets away, the tighter they tuck around your body; sheets re-tuck themselves under the mattress as you move.
providerRawIdea.visibleTrigger: Luca throws off blanket; it snaps back over him.
providerRawIdea.whyThisObject: Bedsheets are meant to cover; if they actively trap, getting up becomes a wrestling match.
providerRawIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to remove sheets causes them to rewrap, preventing standing.
providerRawIdea.frameZeroDescription: Luca lies in bed with one leg out, but the sheet has wrapped around his leg and is pulling him back toward the mattress.

beats.strategy: Luca sits up and pushes the sheet to the foot of the bed.
beats.visibleConsequence: The sheet springs back and tucks itself under his chin, pinning his arms to his sides.
beats.newInformation: The sheet's fabric is elastic and self-tucking.

beats.strategy: Luca rolls toward the edge to slide out.
beats.visibleConsequence: The sheet rolls with him, winding around his torso like a burrito.
beats.newInformation: Moving doesn't loosen; it increases winding.

beats.strategy: Luca kicks violently to break the wrap.
beats.visibleConsequence: The sheet stretches into ropes that tie his ankles to the bed frame.
beats.newInformation: The sheet can transform into adjustable restraints, comedic but not harmful.

beats.strategy: Luca tries to crawl out from the bottom of the bed.
beats.visibleConsequence: The fitted sheet pops off the mattress and becomes a parachute, dragging him back to the center.
beats.newInformation: The whole sheet detaches and acts as a net.

beats.strategy: Luca calls for help, and Mimi enters to pull him out.
beats.visibleConsequence: The sheet wraps around both of them, tucking them together like a mummy, while the bed bounces.
beats.newInformation: The sheet's tucking extends to anyone who tries to intervene.

providerRawIdea.finalPayoff: The sheet wraps around both of them, tucking them together like a mummy, while the bed bounces.
providerRawIdea.suggestedPayoffFamily: goal blocked by self-tucking / role reversal
providerRawIdea.loopPotential: Any morning, Luca will be held by sheets until the bed decides to release him.
providerRawIdea.providerRationale: Bedsheets' covering function becomes trapping; intuitive because throwing off sheets should free you, not rewrap you.

providerRawIdea.title: Upward Faucet
providerRawIdea.normalExpectation: Water flows downward out of spout into glass.
providerRawIdea.impossibleRule: Water flows upward from the faucet to the ceiling when turned on; turning off causes water to rain down only in the sink area.
providerRawIdea.visibleTrigger: Mimi turns on faucet; water arcs up to ceiling like a fountain.
providerRawIdea.whyThisObject: Faucet relies on gravity to pour water; reversing flow direction makes collection impossible.
providerRawIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to fill glass causes water to go the wrong way, so glass never fills.
providerRawIdea.frameZeroDescription: Mimi holds a glass under a faucet, but a vertical stream of water shoots upward to the ceiling, and none falls into the glass.

beats.strategy: Mimi holds the glass above the faucet, upside down, to catch the upward stream.
beats.visibleConsequence: The water flows into the glass but immediately shoots out the top like a second fountain, emptying it.
beats.newInformation: The water's upward momentum continues through any container.

beats.strategy: Mimi turns the faucet off and collects the falling rainwater that comes down.
beats.visibleConsequence: The rain falls directly around the sink but not into the glass, and the glass itself floats upward.
beats.newInformation: When faucet is off, water falls, but the glass becomes buoyant and rises away.

beats.strategy: Mimi puts a lid on the glass and stands on a chair to catch water at ceiling level.
beats.visibleConsequence: The water pressure pushes the lid off, and the glass sticks to the ceiling, filling with water but inaccessible.
beats.newInformation: The ceiling acts as a reservoir; water gathers there and traps containers.

beats.strategy: Mimi uses a bucket and mop to sweep water from ceiling down.
beats.visibleConsequence: The bucket also floats up and sticks to ceiling, splashing water everywhere but down.
beats.newInformation: Objects near the upward flow become anti-gravity and collect on ceiling.

beats.strategy: Mimi calls Luca to help, and he turns the faucet valve under the sink.
beats.visibleConsequence: The water stops, and all the ceiling water falls at once, filling the room waist-deep and floating the glass to Mimi.
beats.newInformation: Shutting off the valve releases the accumulated water all at once, causing a flood but delivering the glass.

providerRawIdea.finalPayoff: The water stops, and all the ceiling water falls at once, filling the room waist-deep and floating the glass to Mimi.
providerRawIdea.loopPotential: Any future faucet use causes ceiling reservoir and eventual indoor rain.
providerRawIdea.providerRationale: Faucet's gravity-driven flow reversed into upward fountain; direct block to filling glass.

providerRawIdea.title: Accelerating Ball
providerRawIdea.normalExpectation: Thrown ball travels to friend and can be caught.
providerRawIdea.impossibleRule: Any throw causes the ball to accelerate away from the thrower, gaining speed with distance, until it orbits back and hits nothing.
providerRawIdea.visibleTrigger: Luca throws gently; ball shoots off and disappears over horizon, then returns like a rocket.
providerRawIdea.whyThisObject: Ball's purpose is to be thrown and caught; if it accelerates uncontrollably, catch is impossible.
providerRawIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The throwing action intended to send ball to friend instead accelerates it away, preventing catch.
providerRawIdea.frameZeroDescription: Luca's arm is extended in a throwing motion, but the ball is already a blur leaving a trail, while Kiko stands empty-handed far away.

beats.strategy: Luca throws the ball as softly as possible.
beats.visibleConsequence: The ball still zooms off, curving around a tree and smashing into a fence, then bounces back at high speed.
beats.newInformation: The ball's acceleration is independent of throw force.

beats.strategy: Kiko runs to intercept the returning ball.
beats.visibleConsequence: The ball swerves around Kiko, gaining more speed, and orbits the yard in a loop.
beats.newInformation: The ball actively avoids being caught.

beats.strategy: Luca and Kiko stand back-to-back and each holds a glove to trap the ball.
beats.visibleConsequence: The ball bounces between their gloves, never being caught, and knocks them both over.
beats.newInformation: The ball treats gloves as new launch pads, increasing chaos.

beats.strategy: Luca tries to trap the ball with a bucket.
beats.visibleConsequence: The ball ricochets off the bucket's rim, accelerates to supersonic speed, and creates a sonic boom.
beats.newInformation: The ball's speed now breaks sound barrier, making it uncatchable and noisy.

beats.strategy: Both give up and walk away.
beats.visibleConsequence: The ball, losing speed, lands gently in Kiko's open hand, then falls asleep with a snore.
beats.newInformation: The ball only becomes catchable when no one is trying to catch it.

providerRawIdea.finalPayoff: The ball, losing speed, lands gently in Kiko's open hand, then falls asleep with a snore.
providerRawIdea.loopPotential: Any new attempt to play catch restarts the acceleration; the ball only cooperates when ignored.
providerRawIdea.providerRationale: Ball's projectile motion is exaggerated into self-acceleration; intuitive and blocks catch.

providerRawIdea.title: Opposite Autocorrect
providerRawIdea.impossibleRule: The phone autocorrects every word to its opposite meaning (e.g., 'yes' becomes 'no', '5' becomes 'five thousand'), and sends instantly before you can edit.
providerRawIdea.visibleTrigger: Luca types 'Meet at 5' and message sends as 'Melt at five thousand'.
providerRawIdea.whyThisObject: Phone's autocorrect is supposed to help, but if it inverts meaning, communication is reversed.
providerRawIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action of texting the plan sends the opposite plan, so friend goes to wrong place/time.
providerRawIdea.frameZeroDescription: Luca looks at phone screen; the sent message reads 'Melt at five thousand' while the intended message is visible above as typed but crossed out.

beats.strategy: Luca types double negatives to get positive meaning.
beats.visibleConsequence: The phone autocorrects to opposite of double negative, resulting in confusing triple negative and message sends 'I won't not never meet'.
beats.newInformation: Inversion is literal but compounds with grammar.

beats.strategy: Luca uses emojis instead of words.
beats.visibleConsequence: Emojis flip to their opposites: thumbs up becomes thumbs down, smiley becomes angry.
beats.newInformation: The autocorrect applies to all symbols, not just text.

beats.strategy: Luca calls instead of texting.
beats.visibleConsequence: His voice comes out reversed, saying 'Meet at five' as 'Evif ta teem', and the friend hears gibberish.
beats.newInformation: The phone's inversion extends to audio, reversing speech.

beats.strategy: Luca uses a different phone, borrowing Mimi's.
beats.visibleConsequence: Mimi's phone also autocorrects, sending 'Don't meet' but then the original phone sends the correct text spontaneously.
beats.newInformation: The rule follows Luca, not the device; only the first phone can sometimes correct itself.

beats.strategy: Luca tries to edit the sent message by appending 'ignore previous', but that also inverts.
beats.visibleConsequence: The friend receives a series of contradictory messages and finally shows up at 5 AM, throwing a pillow at Luca.
beats.newInformation: The accumulation of opposite texts leads to the friend arriving at opposite time.

providerRawIdea.finalPayoff: The friend receives a series of contradictory messages and finally shows up at 5 AM, throwing a pillow at Luca.
providerRawIdea.loopPotential: Any future text will be reversed, forcing Luca to speak in person or use smoke signals.
providerRawIdea.providerRationale: Phone autocorrect is meant to fix errors; reversing meaning creates direct goal interference.

providerRawIdea.title: Relocking Key
providerRawIdea.normalExpectation: Turning key unlocks door so it opens.
providerRawIdea.impossibleRule: The key unlocks the door for exactly one second, then the door locks itself and spins the key back to locked; any attempt to open during that second causes the door to lock harder.
providerRawIdea.visibleTrigger: Arda turns key, hears click, but when he pushes, the door relocks and key spins back.
providerRawIdea.whyThisObject: Key is meant to disengage lock; if the lock re-engages instantly, unlocking is futile.
providerRawIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to unlock door results in immediate relocking, preventing entry.
providerRawIdea.frameZeroDescription: Arda stands at front door with key in lock, door visibly ajar for an instant, but the deadbolt is sliding back into locked position.

beats.strategy: Arda turns key and immediately kicks door open.
beats.visibleConsequence: The door opens a crack, then slams shut with such force that the key snaps in the lock.
beats.newInformation: Force against the door strengthens the relocking.

beats.strategy: Arda turns key and holds it in the unlocked position, waiting.
beats.visibleConsequence: The lock cylinder starts rotating on its own, spinning the key and twisting Arda's wrist.
beats.newInformation: The lock can overpower the key, turning it back.

beats.strategy: Arda calls Mimi to turn the key from inside while he pushes.
beats.visibleConsequence: The key turns, the door unlocks, but then a chain lock appears and locks itself across the door.
beats.newInformation: The lock can generate additional locking mechanisms to stay shut.

beats.strategy: Arda removes the key and tries to pick the lock with a credit card.
beats.visibleConsequence: The card is swallowed by the lock and spit out as a metal key that unlocks a different door across the street.
beats.newInformation: The lock redirects unlocking attempts to other doors, not this one.

beats.strategy: Arda gives up and walks around to the back door.
beats.visibleConsequence: The front door unlocks itself and swings open, then locks Arda inside a small porch as he steps through.
beats.newInformation: The door only opens when no one is trying, and then traps the person.

providerRawIdea.finalPayoff: The front door unlocks itself and swings open, then locks Arda inside a small porch as he steps through.
providerRawIdea.suggestedPayoffFamily: goal reached but new problem / self-trapping
providerRawIdea.loopPotential: Any future unlock attempt will trigger relocking; the door may lock him in or out unpredictably.
providerRawIdea.providerRationale: Key's unlocking function is reversed by instant relocking; visually clear with bolt sliding back.

providerRawIdea.title: Opposite-Side Butter Knife
providerRawIdea.normalExpectation: Spreading butter with knife covers the top surface.
providerRawIdea.impossibleRule: The knife transfers butter to the opposite side of the bread (bottom) regardless of which side you spread; when you flip the bread, the butter flips back to the original top, leaving bottom clean.
providerRawIdea.visibleTrigger: Arda spreads butter on top; the top remains clean, but butter oozes out from the bottom.
providerRawIdea.whyThisObject: Knife's function is to apply spread to the intended surface; transferring to opposite side prevents the usual toast.
providerRawIdea.goalRuleRelationship: The action to butter one side results in butter on the other, so the intended side never gets butter.
providerRawIdea.frameZeroDescription: Arda holds a bread slice with knife mid-spread on top, but a thick layer of butter is visibly dripping from the underside.

beats.strategy: Arda flips the bread over and butters the now-top side, which is currently buttered bottom.
beats.visibleConsequence: The butter on the bottom jumps to the new top, leaving both sides alternately buttered and unbuttered in a loop.
beats.newInformation: Flipping only relocates the butter, not both sides buttered.

beats.strategy: Arda holds the bread vertically and spreads on the edge.
beats.visibleConsequence: Butter appears on the far edge, not the edge he's spreading, and drips onto his hand.
beats.newInformation: The knife transfers spread to the antipodal point on the bread.

beats.strategy: Arda uses a different knife, a spoon.
beats.visibleConsequence: The butter still ends up on the opposite side, and the spoon starts spinning, flinging butter across the kitchen.
beats.newInformation: The rule is tied to the act of spreading, not the knife.

beats.strategy: Arda butters both sides at once using two knives.
beats.visibleConsequence: Both knives transfer butter to each other's faces, leaving the bread dry and the knives coated.
beats.newInformation: Simultaneous spreading causes cross-transfer between tools.

beats.strategy: Arda gives up and eats the bread plain.
beats.visibleConsequence: The butter from the underside levitates and lands on his nose, then the bread flips and butters itself perfectly on both sides.
beats.newInformation: The bread can butter itself only when Arda stops trying, achieving the goal but with a mess.

providerRawIdea.finalPayoff: The butter from the underside levitates and lands on his nose, then the bread flips and butters itself perfectly on both sides.
providerRawIdea.loopPotential: Any future buttering attempt will cause butter on wrong side until he stops, then it self-corrects.
providerRawIdea.providerRationale: Knife's spreading action is spatially inverted to opposite side; visually clear with butter dripping from bottom.
